deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 28 continues a set of German lecture or reading notes on the geography and history of ancient Egypt (Lower, Middle and Upper Egypt, Memphis), probably school or university notes. The hand and content suggest a student copy rather than Gauss's research papers. The bundle label 'Lagrange1816' does not match the content.

Content, paraphrased:
(1) Memphis extends south to the temples of Vulcan (Ptah) and Apis.
(2) Near Memphis stand the great monuments still extant.
  - I. Pyramids: the largest are near Cairo, and about 40 are counted in that region. The greatest, associated with Cheops, is said to be 800 Fuß high, each side of the base equal to the height. It is built of squared stones in steps so that one can climb it, and it is the only one that is opened/entered.
  - II. Labyrinth, near Lake Moeris: 12 great palaces connected to one another under a common roof, 6 facing north and 6 facing south. They were divided into halls, courts and chambers, half above ground and half below. In total 3000 rooms, 1500 above and 1500 below ground. Descending from the top required 300 (more likely 360) steps. Built entirely of stone, with decorated walls.
(3) According to Gatterer (Johann Christoph Gatterer, Göttingen historian), it was a temple of the Sun. It was symbolic: it represented the Sun's course through the zodiac. The next page continues: 12 halls = 12 signs, half above and half below the equator, 360 = degrees of the zodiac.

The only 'computations' are trivial counts: 1500 + 1500 = 3000 and 6 + 6 = 12. There is also the stated equality of pyramid height and base side.
errors: Not a mathematical error: the stated pyramid height of 800 Fuß and the claim that the base side equals the height are factually wrong. The Great Pyramid is about 146 m high, roughly 450 Paris feet, with a base side of about 230 m. These figures are typical exaggerations of 18th-century compendia, not the writer's slip.
The number of steps is transcribed as 300. Comparison with the next page (360 = degrees of the zodiac) suggests the intended figure is 360.

results.what: Descriptive historical notes on Egyptian pyramids and the Labyrinth of Lake Moeris, citing Gatterer's symbolic-astronomical interpretation (12 palaces = 12 zodiac signs, 360 steps = 360 degrees)
results.usually_credited_to: Herodotus (Labyrinth description); J. C. Gatterer (zodiacal interpretation, late 18th c.)

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics, only conventional school or lecture notes on ancient Egyptian history drawn from Gatterer-style compendia. It is probably not even Gauss's own work.

checkable.asserts: The Labyrinth's 3000 rooms split as 1500 above ground and 1500 below.
The 12 palaces split as 6 facing north and 6 facing south.
12 zodiac signs of 30 degrees each give the 360 steps/degrees of the symbolic interpretation (next page).

transcription_corrections: 'Dieses ist die einzige die gestuft[?] ist' should more likely read 'die einzige die geöffnet ist' (the only one opened/entered).
'Erbaut unter[?] Psammetich[?] an dem Mörissee' is doubtful. The image seems closer to 'Es lag ... von dem See Möris' (located by Lake Moeris), with no mention of Psammetich.
'300 Stufen' is likely '360 Stufen', consistent with the next page's '360 ... Grade des Thierkreises'.
'aber eigentlich[?] kein bildlicher[?] Tempel' is more likely 'aber eigentlich ein symbolischer Tempel'.
The final words 'an den [?]' likely read 'andeuten' (to indicate the Sun's course through the zodiac), continuing onto the next page.
Line 4 'und waren [?] sind los[?]' and line 5 'einmal[?] Gegen[?] weiß[?]' remain uncertain. The sense is that many pyramids are counted in that region.
